- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility events.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term mean reversion.
- Overshoots after price spikes (e.g., 68+ → 69+ forecast) are common, leading to overestimation of subsequent days.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or when historical mean is lower than recent highs.
- Forecasts show weak sensitivity to recent low prices — fails to “catch” bottoming out or mean-reversion triggers.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values when historical 30-day average is above 65, and underestimates when below 60.
- Forecasts often fail to adjust for seasonal or calendar-driven patterns (e.g., end-of-month or quarter effects) — may need to incorporate time-of-year or day-of-week features.
- Model tends to overfit recent volatility, leading to overreaction to short-term noise rather than structural trends.
